dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: dehāntare tvagvibhāgam bhittibhūtaṃ vicintayet | na kiṃcid antare tasya dhyāyann adhyeyabhāg bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: Let one think of the skin of the body as a wall, with nothing at all inside it. Meditating in this way, one comes to share in what cannot be meditated upon.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: everyone habitually identifies with the body; detaching consciousness from its limits develops a sense of all-pervasiveness, and when that is reached there is no longer an object to meditate on, as Bhairava says in verse 16. Wallis: the 'dividing wall' of skin is merely a screen with nothing within.
dharana.technique_name: The Skin as a Wall with Nothing Inside
dharana.instruction: Feel the skin as a thin wall and the inside of the body as an empty room.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 25' = verse 48 (agrees with Singh)
The Mystery Within (2019), parallel translations: 'Dharana 25 • verso 48' (agrees)

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 48 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the skin as a thin wall
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a thin boundary (the skin) around empty space, like a wall around an empty room.
geometry.svg_hint: a body outline drawn as a single thin line, the inside left blank
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Empty room
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the body is felt as a thin wall around nothing, and the thing to meditate on falls away. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Feel the skin as a thin boundary and the inside as empty
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The skin all around the body, felt as a thin wall

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Let one think of the skin of the body as a wall, with nothing at all inside it. Meditating in this way, one comes to share in what cannot be meditated upon.
adiyogi.method_summary: Feel the skin all over the body as a thin wall, like the walls of a room. Imagine there is nothing inside it at all. Rest in that emptiness without looking for anything in it.

honesty.disclosure: Door 025 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 25 (verse 48) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 025 is dharana 25, verse 48. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If the image feels unsettling, rest the attention on the breath or the feet instead. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Breath

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Feel the skin all around you as a thin wall. Inside, nothing at all. Rest there.

beats.title: Reaction cue

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 48: think of the skin as a wall with nothing inside it; meditating so, one reaches what cannot be meditated on.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.
